hook.text: In 1964, Kitty Genovese was attacked in New York while 38 neighbors reportedly watched and did nothing.

buildup.text: The bystander effect: the more people present, the less likely any individual is to help. Responsibility diffuses.

discovery.text: Each person assumes someone else will act. If no one acts, each person concludes action must not be needed.

twist.text: The original Genovese story was exaggerated by media. But the bystander effect is real and repeatedly confirmed in.

climax.text: In groups, responsibility must be assigned, not assumed. Point at one person and say help me.

punchline.text: Everyone watches, nobody acts. Diffused responsibility freezes entire crowds.

quiz.question: What causes the bystander effect?
options: Responsibility diffuses in groups so each person assumes someone else will act
